newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - NOV 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - NOV 4.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - This year's GDP growth is not expected to exceed last year's 4.8 percent according to the Czech Statistical Bureau. GDP should grow 5.1 to 5.6 percent in 1997 with inflation falling by one percentage point to 7.5 percent.

- An association of creditors of the bankrupt Ceska Banka intends to sue the Czech National Bank. The association, representing 300 creditors owed 50 million crowns, is accusing the National Bank of neglect.
- Komercni Banka has posted a net profit of 4.9 billion crowns in the first three quarters of 1996.
- Tourism generated record receipts in the main tourist season this year, the Ministry for Local Development said.
- The European Union will provide 50 million crowns for the support of Czech exporters through the PHARE programme.
- Nominal wages are expected to increase by 16.2 to 17.2 percent in 1997, a real growth of 8.1 to 8.5 percent, a slight decrease compared with this year.
- The share of the grey market in GDP is approximately between eight and 15 percent. This roughly corresponds to the European average, according to experts.

- Microsoft's sales have been roughly doubling in the time it has been active on the Czech market. In the 1996 fiscal year sales exceeded one billion crowns while a year earlier they were 620 million crowns.
MLADA FRONTA DNES - The steep petrol and diesel price increases have now stopped, according to experts.
- Vladimir Dlouhy, the Minister of Industry of Trade and Industry has proposed importing natural gas from the Netherlands.
PRAVO - The state should keep at least a partial influence in Komercni Banka, a representative from the bank said. The influence should not be active, but rather of a blocking character.
